In its development, although it can be said that the struggle of women has been quite successful, it needs to receive vigilance. This means that women must always be protected from actions that harm them due to their vulnerable condition. Women as a national asset who play a role in the process of continuation and creation of quality generations need to receive guarantees for the fulfillment of their rights and protection from acts of violence and discrimination.
In addition to women needing to be protected, and in their development increasingly being able to protect themselves, women must be empowered. This empowerment is importantly aimed at gender equality, which is a condition of equality for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings so they are able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural activities, national defense and security, and equality in enjoying the results of development.

Article 7
Women victims of acts of violence have the right to obtain protection, information, integrated services, continuous handling up to the rehabilitation stage and confidential handling both from individuals, groups or institutions both Government and Non-Government.

This supports a ‘Yes’ for private-sector engagement. But the retrieved candidates for this indicator did not include Pasal 8–9 at all (retrieval failure). Given only the shown candidates, the judge reasonably said ‘No’; however, the judge’s rationale that there is no mention of businesses is only true because the relevant articles were not retrieved.

Article 14
(1) The implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women in the regions is carried out by establishing, developing, strengthening, or utilizing task forces, forums, working groups or other institutions.
(2) The membership of task forces, forums, working groups, or other institutions as referred to in paragraph (1) consists of relevant Regional Work Units, Community Organizations, Universities, and civil society.
(3) The establishment of task forces, forums, working groups, or other institutions as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be stipulated by Regent's Decree.

CHAPTER VII
MONITORING AND EVALUATION
Article 21
(1) To ensure synergy, continuity, and effectiveness of integrated measures in the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women, the Regional Government conducts monitoring.

(2) Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) is intended to determine progress in the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women in the region.

(3) Monitoring is conducted periodically through coordination and direct monitoring of Regional Work Units that implement policies, programs and activities for the protection of women.

(4) Monitoring is conducted from the planning stage through to the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women for the current year.

Article 22
(1) Evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women is conducted at the end of each fiscal year.

(2) The results of the evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women are used as input material for the formulation of policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women for the following year.

(3) Evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

CHAPTER V
EMPOWERMENT OF WOMEN
Article 18
(1) In order to improve the position, role, and quality of women, as well as efforts to realize equality and gender justice in family life, society, nationhood, and statehood, women must be empowered.
(2) The empowerment of women as referred to in paragraph (1) is directed toward obtaining opportunities and their rights as human beings, to be able to play a role and participate in political, economic, social and cultural activities, national defense and security, and equality in enjoying the results of development.

CHAPTER VIII
FINANCING
Article 23
(1) Funding for the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women in the region is sourced from the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget, and other legitimate sources of income that are non-binding.
(2) In the event that the region receives funding assistance for the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women from the Government, it shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 1
In this Regional Regulation what is meant by:
1. Region is Tapin Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the administration of the Regional Government of Tapin Regency.
3. Regent is the Regent of Tapin.
4. Regional People's Representative Council hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional People's Representative Council of Tapin Regency.
5. Agency is the Agency for Women's Empowerment and Family Planning of Tapin Regency.
6. Head of Agency is the Head of the Agency for Women's Empowerment and Family Planning of Tapin Regency.
7. Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities of men and women that have equality in accordance with the development and socio-cultural conditions of society.
8. Gender-Based Violence is any act of deviation caused by an imbalance in the relations between women and men that results in misery or suffering of women including children whether physically, sexually and/or psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom arbitrarily that occurs in the private/domestic sphere and in the public sphere.
9. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to women carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
10. Women's Empowerment is any effort to improve physical, mental spiritual, social, knowledge, and skills capabilities so that women are ready to be utilized in accordance with their respective abilities.
11. Disability is a permanent physical, mental and intellectual, or sensory disorder.

Article 5
In political matters, women have the right to:
a. vote and/or be elected in general elections, regional head elections, village head elections and/or other political position elections based on equal rights through direct, general, free, secret, honest and fair voting according to the applicable laws and regulations; and
b. be appointed to any government position.

Article 7
Women victims of acts of violence have the right to obtain protection, information, integrated services, continuous handling up to the rehabilitation stage and confidential handling both from individuals, groups or institutions both Government and Non-Government.

7.2.rationale: Pasal 23(2) in Indonesian states: “Dalam hal daerah mendapatkan bantuan pendanaan ... dari Pemerintah ...”. In Indonesian legal drafting, “Pemerintah” (capital P) typically refers to the central/national government (distinct from “Pemerintah Daerah” used throughout for local government). So the judge’s ‘Yes’ (national government funding is a possible source) matches the source text. The golden label ‘No’ appears wrong.
